Down at Portsmouth in the Hampshire's Myles Cottrell beat his own championship best with a 74.40 javelin throw. Myles continued his superb early season form a short while later by launching his spear out to 78.86 while representing the AAA at Loughborough.

Myles Cottrell helped the GB under 23 team to second place in the first ever Under-23 European Cup match at Gateshead, 17/18 July. His 71.36 javelin throw, achieved with his opening effort, placed him second to yet another fine Finnish prospect, Mika Parviainen, who won with 77.26.

Myles Cottrell was bumped off our scheduled flight and sat with the pilots as the next full flight nearly went without him. He was still at 5000 feet as he took advantage of an injured Nigel Bevan to fill the 'A' javelin slot.

Nigel Bevan had started a course of injections, Myles Cottrell had been called to an International Meet in the Ukraine - along with Derek Browne - and we were delighted when Youth Ben Cascoe (who had hurled the senior implement 52m) agreed to join the team at short notice.
Triple jumper Derek Browne fouled the take-off board five times before a 15.42 effort got him up into 4th, while Myles Cottrell's 6th round 71.96 gave him a season's best, just 2cm behind 2nd place.
